issues.legal_issue: Ownership is directly and substantially in issue in a prior injunction suit when the injunction claim and the defence turn on competing claims to ownership, even if no separate issue expressly framed is titled ownership.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought an injunction on the basis that the plaintiff owned the house and had mortgaged it to the co-plaintiff.
The defendant claimed that the plaintiff had relinquished the house to her and the children and disputed the mortgage.
The earlier court considered the mortgage, the alleged settlement, and possession, and found that the settlement had occurred and the wife and children were in possession.
The later claimant sought title and possession as a purchaser from the plaintiff in the earlier suit.
issues.conclusion: The ownership issue was directly and substantially involved in the earlier suit, and its final judgment operates as res judicata against the later title claim brought by the purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a matter directly and substantially in issue between parties or persons claiming under them, and heard and finally decided by a competent court, cannot be tried again. As stated in Sulochana Amma v. Narayan Nair, (1994) 2 SCC 14, when title is in issue in an injunction suit for the purpose of deciding entitlement to the injunction, the decision can operate as res judicata in a later title suit between the same parties or their privies.

rule.if: injunction_suit_between_predecessors and ownership_claim_underlay_injunction and ownership_was_contested and earlier_court_considered_ownership_related_claims and later_title_suit_by_successor

predicates.injunction_suit_between_predecessors: The original parties litigated a suit seeking an injunction.
predicates.ownership_claim_underlay_injunction: The party seeking the injunction relied on ownership as the basis for the requested protection.
predicates.ownership_was_contested: The opposing party asserted a competing claim to ownership of the property.
predicates.earlier_court_considered_ownership_relat: The earlier court considered claims and evidence concerning ownership, the asserted transfer of rights, or possession.
predicates.later_title_suit_by_successor: A person claiming through a party to the earlier suit later brought a suit asserting title to the same property.
predicates.later_title_claim_precluded_by_prior_dec: The later title claim cannot be tried again because the prior judgment is conclusive on the matter.

issues.definition: When an injunction suit between predecessors rests on ownership, ownership is contested and considered, and a successor later sues on title to the same property, the later title claim is precluded by the prior decision.

issues.legal_issue: A later title suit by a successor is barred when the predecessor could and ought to have raised in the earlier suit the ownership-based ground or alternative relief on which the later claim depends.
material_facts: In the earlier suit, the wife claimed that the husband had relinquished his rights in the house and that she and the children occupied it under the settlement.
The husband claimed through an inherited interest in a house allotted to his mother, although the formal conveyance in his favour was obtained later.
The husband and the co-plaintiff sought an injunction based on the mortgage but did not alternatively seek possession on the basis of the husband's claimed rights.
The earlier suit was dismissed and was not appealed.
The later claimant purchased the house from the husband and sought title and possession.
issues.conclusion: The later purchaser's claim was also barred by constructive res judicata because the ownership-based claim and alternative claim for possession could and ought to have been raised in the earlier suit.
issues.legal_principle: Explanation IV to section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure deems a matter that might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence in the former suit to have been directly and substantially in issue there. The court applied this principle to the successor claiming through the earlier plaintiff; it also relied on the rule in Sulochana Amma v. Narayan Nair, (1994) 2 SCC 14, concerning the effect of an earlier injunction decision where title was in issue.

rule.if: earlier_suit_between_predecessors and later_title_suit_by_successor and predecessor_had_ownership_based_claim and opposing_party_asserted_competing_right and alternative_possession_claim_was_available and omitted_claim_could_and_ought_to_have_been_raised

predicates.earlier_suit_between_predecessors: The parties through whom the later claimant and opposing party claim litigated an earlier suit concerning the same property.
predicates.later_title_suit_by_successor: A person claiming through a party to the earlier suit later brought a suit asserting title to the property.
predicates.predecessor_had_ownership_based_claim: The predecessor relied on an existing or claimed right to the property as a basis for relief in the earlier suit.
predicates.opposing_party_asserted_competing_right: The opposing party in the earlier suit asserted a competing right to the property.
predicates.alternative_possession_claim_was_availab: The predecessor could have sought possession as an alternative form of relief based on the claimed right to the property.
predicates.omitted_claim_could_and_ought_to_have_be: The ownership-based ground or alternative relief was available and should have been advanced in the earlier suit but was not.
predicates.later_claim_precluded_as_omitted_ground: The later claim cannot be pursued because it depends on a ground that should have been raised in the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a successor brings a title suit after an earlier property suit in which the predecessor had a property-based claim and an available alternative claim that should have been raised, the later claim is precluded as an omitted ground.
